scope: Explicit board HTTP Date sampling and existing model POST cancellation/deadline ownership

api.loopback: 127.0.0.1 only when allow_loopback=True is explicitly passed both for fixture source construction and refresh
api.redirects: Every non-200 status rejected; HTTPConnection does not follow redirects
verification: Actual connected peer equals configured literal IPv4 and port
Exactly one Date, Content-Type and Content-Length; no Transfer-Encoding
application/json body of declared exact positive size, at most 65536 bytes
Unique JSON keys, finite JSON values, protocol_version integer 1, ok true, role model_inference_only
Only the exact immutable HttpDateSample built from this verified response is authorized once; the proof is cleared in finally
boot_id comes from the board StableTimelineClock, never a Windows/server/session/generation identifier
timing: sent_monotonic sampled before connect; received_monotonic sampled immediately after response headers
Client and StableTimelineClock must share the same monotonic callable
Clock writer wait_timeout is min(0.25, original remaining deadline); cancellation/deadline also supplied to clock writer
No retry or fresh inference budget; no implicit Date refresh on LLM/TTS POST

caller_example: timeline = StableTimelineClock(board_linux_boot_id, sampler.health_date_source_id(), sampler.validate_sample, monotonic=sampler.clock, utc_bounds=trusted_utc_bounds, server_error_seconds=configured_error_seconds, anchor_path=board_private_anchor_path)
Use timeline.event_time for board events. At an existing idle refresh point, refresh before entering any compaction_guard/SQLite transaction.

On refresh busy/error/expiry, do not retry with a larger deadline or substitute board wall time; skip this compaction attempt and let the clock retain/degrade its existing anchor according to its policy.
Only after successful refresh and safe_for_compaction may existing short store prepare/commit operations take the clock quality lease; never retain that lease across HTTP/model work.
trust_limit: Literal IP/port, endpoint role and one-shot response binding constrain the configured trusted LAN source. They are not cryptographic authentication and do not measure Windows clock accuracy; UTC bounds and server-error assumptions remain explicit caller policy.
socket_fix: Both POST and Date retain and control the same actual connected socket. A minimal close-deferring socket facade prevents HTTPConnection.getresponse(Connection: close) from invalidating that control while HTTPResponse still reads its makefile. The original deadline/cancellation watcher shuts down the actual socket; request finally closes response, connection and socket. No new server or nonblocking transport framework.

audio_review.current_ram_pcm: 24000Hz mono pcm_s16le; native non-24k or non-1D waves rejected, no rate conversion
audio_review.playback_plan: Generic plan preserves native rate, but current actual model plan is 24k mono. Default legacy player bridge must reject non-24k without an explicit reviewed converter; preserve native frozen receipts. A 48k stereo final sink does not redefine model PCM or receipt sample units.
audio_review.separate_fixed_conversion: Existing echo-cancel reference branch converts 24k mono to 16k; this is not model output or playback-plan resampling.

validation.coverage: Date source/peer/framing/role/boot/mono verification, one-shot proof, POST no implicit refresh, controlled fake slow headers/body deadline and cancellation for POST and Date, detached conn.sock shutdown ownership, original remaining clock-writer wait
